title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a short programme of questions ('À examiner'). It is written on recycled IBM/CRAY line-printer paper; the struck-out JCL header '//EXEC PGM=IEFBR14' is not mathematics. It continues the previous page. There Grothendieck takes a smooth curve X of type (g,ν) over Q̄ and a stable singular curve Y of the same type with a 'propagateur' N, i.e. smoothing or log data at the nodes. He forms the 'modified' fundamental group π1([Y,N]), which is in effect the log fundamental group, isomorphic to the π1 of a nearby smooth fibre. He then compares the two groups via a Teichmüller isomorphism.

(a) Can the fundamental anabelian conjecture (the isomorphism/Hom conjecture for hyperbolic curves over finitely generated fields) be extended from smooth hyperbolic curves to singular anabelian curves? He means stable curves with normal 'propagateur', i.e. pointed stable log curves, whose arithmetic π1 is π1([Y,N]) together with the outer action of π1(K) = Gal(K̄/K).

(b) Take a singular anabelian Y over a field K finitely generated over Q. Can one recover group-theoretically, from π1(Y) with its outer π1(K)-action, the set Sing(Y) ∪ P (nodes plus marked points or cusps)? The proposed description is as conjugacy classes of subgroups of the geometric π1 that are isomorphic to Ẑ and normalized by π1(K). On such subgroups Galois automatically acts through the cyclotomic character, i.e. they are Ẑ(1)'s.
- Cusps correspond to inertia subgroups.
- Nodes correspond to vanishing-cycle (edge) subgroups.
This matches the previous page's remark about distinguished conjugacy classes of homomorphisms Ẑ(1) → π1(X).

(c) Taking the Mumford–Deligne compactification of M_{g,ν} as model, define an 'anabelian compactification' of a smooth anabelian variety over a field of characteristic 0 (WLOG finitely generated over Q). Ask how it behaves under specialization. The idea is a boundary whose strata are again anabelian and are detected by Ẑ(1)-type inertia data in π1, as the boundary of M̄_{g,ν} is detected by Dehn twists.

The next page (presentations of Teichmüller groupoids by pants, Lego pieces and reflections) shows the context: the Teichmüller tower and its Galois action, i.e. the Esquisse programme.
errors: In (b), 'subgroups isomorphic to Ẑ normalized by π1(K)' is too weak as stated. Open subgroups nẐ of a cuspidal or nodal inertia group are also such subgroups. One needs maximality (or commensurator-closure) to get a bijection with Sing(Y) ∪ P.

The question only makes sense for the log/'propagator' fundamental group π1([Y,N]) with a Galois action defined over K. The plain étale π1 of a nodal curve does not contain nodal Ẑ(1)'s: nodes there produce loops in the dual graph instead. The previous page itself notes that the Teichmüller identification π1(X) ≅ π1([Y,N]) is not Galois-equivariant, so the Galois action must be taken intrinsically on [Y,N].

The condition as written does not separate cusps from nodes: both kinds of inertia carry cyclotomic action. Telling them apart needs extra structure, as later combinatorial anabelian geometry shows (e.g. how the subgroups sit relative to vertex subgroups).

ideas.what: Extend the anabelian (isomorphism) conjecture from smooth hyperbolic curves to stable/log-stable curves with smoothing data
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian geometry of pointed stable log curves; combinatorial anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: S. Mochizuki ('Semi-graphs of anabelioids', 2006; work on log/stable curves); Hoshi–Mochizuki (combinatorial anabelian geometry, 2009–)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) and Esquisse state the smooth case; the singular/stable extension is not stated there as far as I know

ideas.what: Group-theoretic recovery of cusps and nodes as (maximal) Ẑ-subgroups of the geometric π1 normalized by Galois, with Galois acting via the cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: Group-theoretic characterization of cuspidal/nodal inertia subgroups (weight argument)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Nakamura (cuspidal inertia, ~1990); Mochizuki, Hoshi–Mochizuki (nodal/edge subgroups, 'IPSC'-type Galois actions)

ideas.what: Define an 'anabelian compactification' of a smooth anabelian variety, modelled on Mumford–Deligne M̄_{g,ν}, and study its specialization
ideas.modern_name: No standard notion; nearest are log-smooth/toroidal compactifications of hyperbolic polycurves and configuration spaces, and log-specialization of fundamental groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart; related work by Mochizuki, Hoshi (hyperbolic polycurves), Tamagawa/Mochizuki (specialization)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly proposes extending the fundamental anabelian conjecture to stable singular curves endowed with smoothing ('propagateur') data, over fields finitely generated over Q. This is a log-stable anabelian conjecture formulated about 1984.
missed.quote: Extension de la conjecture fondamentale sur gr. alg. anabéliens aux courbes anabéliennes singulières (stables, avec propagateur normal)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the log-stable direction of Mochizuki's work and the combinatorial anabelian programme by over a decade. A clean Isom/Hom theorem for pointed stable log curves over number fields (not just p-adic or combinatorial versions) is, as far as I know, not stated in this generality.

missed.claim: He gives the cyclotomic-normalizer criterion for recovering cusps and nodes from the arithmetic fundamental group, around 6 years before Nakamura's published characterization of cuspidal inertia subgroups. It already includes nodes, which only entered the literature with combinatorial anabelian geometry.
missed.quote: est-il vrai qu'on récupère les cl. de Sing(Y) ∪ P marqués en termes des classes de conj. de sous-groupes de π1(Y), isom. à Ẑ, et normalisés par π1(K) (l'opération de π1(K) dessus se faisant automatiquement via le caractère cyclotomique)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point: the idea is posed as a question, not proved, so 'finished' is generous. It shows Grothendieck viewed the boundary of the Teichmüller tower anabelianly, through Ẑ(1)-inertia.

missed.claim: He proposes a general notion of 'anabelian compactification' of smooth anabelian varieties on the model of M̄_{g,ν}, together with a study of specialization.
missed.quote: S'inspirer des compactifications MD des M_{g,ν}, définir ce que c'est qu'une compactification anabélienne d'une variété lisse anabélienne ... Comportement par spécialisation ???
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: There is no standard such notion today. A definition singling out compactifications whose boundary strata are anabelian and detected by Galois-cyclotomic inertia could unify work on hyperbolic polycurves, configuration spaces and the Grothendieck–Teichmüller boundary behaviour.

deep.surprise_reason: These are questions, not results, but they are early and precise. They state the cyclotomic-inertia recovery of cusps and nodes and a log-stable anabelian conjecture before Nakamura (1990) and long before Hoshi–Mochizuki. The 'anabelian compactification' idea remains undeveloped. The core directions were later realized independently, so the surprise is modest.
transcription_corrections: '(stables, ou plus généralement normales[?])' should read '(stables, avec propagateur normal)', consistent with the previous page's 'propagateur normal N'.
'Sing(Y) ∪ P manquants[?]' is more likely 'Sing(Y) ∪ P marqués' (marked points); 'Y_∞' is written under P as an alternative description of the points at infinity.

'classes de conj.' is written at the start of the line, replacing the struck 'sous-groupes'; read 'en termes des classes de conj. de sous-groupes de π1(Y)'. Likewise 'est normalisés' should read 'normalisés'.
The JCL header (JOB=CRAY2 ... EXEC PGM=IEFBR14) is pre-printed on recycled computer paper and crossed out, not written by Grothendieck.
